1.label: Easy
1.focus: recognise vocabulary, meaning and simple grammar

2.label: Intermediate
2.focus: apply reading and grammar skills in context

standard.label: Terminale
standard.style: clear English at final-year secondary level

ultra_simple.label: Very simple
ultra_simple.style: very accessible English with occasional French support

concepts.title: Personal information and document vocabulary

explanations.standard: This unit uses a core set of words for personal information and official documents: biometric, passport, processing time, minor, appointment, expired, in person and document.
explanations.simple: Learn the words that help you understand forms and official documents: passport, appointment, minor, expired, document and others.
explanations.ultra_simple: These are the key words of the unit. Example: 'expired' means no longer valid; 'appointment' means an arranged meeting.

common_mistakes: confusing 'appointment' with a document
confusing 'expired' with 'missing'
using 'in person' as if it meant 'online'

concepts.title: Listening for specific information

explanations.standard: The unit asks you to listen for precise details and judge yes/no statements about what you hear.
explanations.simple: Listen for the exact detail you need. Do not try to remember every word.
explanations.ultra_simple: Listen like a detective: one question, one detail. En français : cherche l'information précise, pas tout le texte.

common_mistakes: guessing from general knowledge instead of the listening source
answering without checking the exact statement

concepts.title: Speech practice

explanations.standard: The unit includes pronunciation practice and tongue twisters to rehearse problematic English sounds.
explanations.simple: Read slowly first, then repeat more smoothly. Focus on the target sounds.
explanations.ultra_simple: Say it slowly, then faster. The goal is clear pronunciation, not speed.

common_mistakes: rushing before producing sounds clearly
treating pronunciation practice as a spelling exercise

concepts.title: Predicting before reading

explanations.standard: Before detailed reading, use the title, subheadings, bold or capitalised words and quick skimming to anticipate the likely content.
explanations.simple: Look at the title and important-looking words before reading every sentence.
explanations.ultra_simple: First look at the big clues. Then guess what the text is about. Après, tu lis en détail.

common_mistakes: reading every sentence before identifying the topic
ignoring headings and visually prominent words

concepts.title: Reading a formal administrative form

explanations.standard: A formal form is organised into labelled sections. Read the heading of each section first, then locate the precise field or document requested.
explanations.simple: Use the section headings to find the right information quickly.
explanations.ultra_simple: A form is like a map: first choose the right section, then the right box.

common_mistakes: reading a field without checking its section
confusing personal details with supporting documents

concepts.title: Accuracy and integrity in formal forms

explanations.standard: The sample form includes a declaration that the information is correct and the submitted documents are genuine.
explanations.simple: Formal forms must be completed carefully with correct information.
explanations.ultra_simple: Do not invent information on a form. Check your details before you sign.

common_mistakes: guessing missing details
signing before checking required information

concepts.title: Vocabulary in a formal notice

explanations.standard: The vocabulary activity uses the words proposed, bride, bridegroom, celebrant, notice and solemnise in the context of a marriage notice.
explanations.simple: These words help you understand the sample formal notice and its context.
explanations.ultra_simple: Learn each word with its job in the notice: people, action or document.

common_mistakes: confusing bride with bridegroom
confusing celebrant with notice

concepts.title: Coordinating and subordinating conjunctions

explanations.standard: Coordinating conjunctions join independent clauses. Subordinating conjunctions connect a dependent clause to an independent clause.
explanations.simple: Conjunctions link ideas. Some join equal clauses; others introduce conditions, reasons, time or contrast.
explanations.ultra_simple: A conjunction is a bridge between ideas. 'and' adds; 'but' contrasts; 'if' gives a condition; 'because' gives a reason.

common_mistakes: using 'although' where a condition is needed
using 'unless' as if it meant 'because'
joining ideas without checking their relationship

concepts.title: Passive voice

explanations.standard: The passive voice puts the receiver of the action in subject position. A common pattern is a form of 'be' followed by a past participle.
explanations.simple: In the passive, focus on what receives the action: 'The form was completed.'
explanations.ultra_simple: Active: someone does the action. Passive: the thing receiving the action comes first.

common_mistakes: forgetting 'be' after a modal
using the base verb instead of the past participle

concepts.title: Completing an application carefully

explanations.standard: The writing task asks you to understand the requested information, complete the application truthfully and sign it.
explanations.simple: Read every field, give accurate information and remember the signature.
explanations.ultra_simple: Read → check → fill in → sign. Ne devine jamais une information officielle.

common_mistakes: leaving required information unchecked
using invented information in a real administrative context
forgetting the signature field

adaptive_rules: After two errors on the same concept, suggest Simple English.
After one additional error, suggest Very simple.
After three consecutive correct answers, suggest a higher difficulty.
Explanation level and exercise difficulty remain independent.
Use the learner's first name only occasionally.
